preconditions.description: The number of cities is between 2 and 10^5, inclusive.
The number of roads is between n - 1 and 10^5, inclusive.
Each road connects two distinct cities between 1 and n, inclusive.
No road connects a city to itself.

preconditions.expression: For any pair of cities, there is at most one road connecting them.
preconditions.description: The graph is a simple, undirected graph without self-loops or multiple edges.

preconditions.expression: One can reach any city from every other city.

postconditions.expression: The output is a list of n - 1 integers.
postconditions.description: Each integer is the remainder of the smallest number Koala could have written for the corresponding destination city.

postconditions.expression: The smallest number for destination i+1 is the concatenation of the road numbers on the shortest path from city 1 to city i+2.
postconditions.description: The output represents the minimum possible number Koala could have written for each destination city.
The remainders of the smallest numbers are computed modulo 10^9+7.
